transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (ZettaWorks Head of ML), Tom Berger (Platform), Priya Menon (Security)

Summary (auto): quick scoping call to pick final POC success criteria between Hosted / Dedicated / Private; agree on workload sizing, baseline benchmarks and timelines. Action items and benchmark plan defined.

Topics (auto): POC success metrics; expected traffic & concurrency; benchmark methodology; security constraints; timeline & next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour, um quick intros please?
[00:12] Anika Rao: hi i m anika, we run the model infra team at zettaworks, we own the ml infra and product integration.
[00:18] Tom Berger: tom - platform, i'll own the deployment side and the infra hooks.
[00:22] Priya Menon: priya - security, i'll be the contact on compliance and encryption.
[00:27] Jorge Alvarez: jorge from redwood, i ll cover benchmarks and the harness.
[00:32] Maya Patel: great. high level goal: pick deployment mode for the POC that balances cost, latency and our compliance needs — and then run a short benchmark to validate.
[00:42] Anika Rao: yes our main things: p50 target for short completions under 150ms, 99 latency under 600, and throughput should support burst to 250 concurrent requests. cost wise we want to understand unit cost, threshold around 0.12 to 0.18 per 1k tokens is our rough target.
[01:05] Tom Berger: to add, we have existing K8s infra and would prefer dedicated if it means simpler network egress and lower latency, but private/on-prem is a hard requirement for some regulated customers so we need to know path to private later.
[01:28] Maya Patel: ok. quick note on definitions — when i say Hosted i mean Redwood API (managed), Dedicated means reserved GPU pools we provision for you, Private means VPC or on-prem with customer-managed control plane.
[01:45] Priya Menon: stop there — for us private/VPC is about KMS integration and cert-based authentication; SOC2 plus audit logs are mandatory for the pilot, at least retention 90 days.
[02:02] Jorge Alvarez: noted. for benchmarks i recommend three runs: latency run (90th/99th percentiles), throughput run (RPS stepping to 250), and burn-rate cost estimation run using your real prompt mix.
[02:22] Anika Rao: question: when you do dedicated benchmarks, do you test with KV cache warm-up scenarios? most of our traffic is chat-like with repeated prefixes.
[02:35] Jorge Alvarez: yes, we will run cold and warm kv cache variants. sometimes the transcriber messes our product name — but the harness uses prefix caching and we can show you delta on tokens per request.
[02:50] Maya Patel: also we should test quantized model variants, some customers trade a bit of quality for 2-3x cost savings. what quality guardrails do you want?
[03:02] Anika Rao: we have an eval set and acceptance is: F1 drop < 2% on entity extraction and hallucination rate under 1% measured on sampled responses.
[03:17] Tom Berger: ops question: for Dedicated do you do autoscaling or fixed pools during the POC? we need to know if we must provision slack capacity.
[03:29] Jorge Alvarez: dedicated supports autoscaling with policy knobs; for the benchmark we usually provision a stable pool to get consistent numbers then run autoscale tests during stress windows.
[03:42] Priya Menon: about data residency: some EU customers require model outputs not leave eu-west1, can Redwood route by region?
[03:52] Maya Patel: yes routing by region is supported for Hosted and Dedicated; Private obviously stays in your VPC/on-prem. a caveat: some model variants are only available in certain regions — we'll surface that in the catalog.
[04:10] Anika Rao: we also need end-to-end tracing to correlate token cost per request to user id, is that possible?
[04:20] Jorge Alvarez: yes console provides token-level breakdowns and tracing hooks, we can also ship logs to your SIEM; note there are PII redaction options if you want.
[04:33] Tom Berger: about SLOs — do you have SLA numbers for Dedicated or hosted during POC?
[04:40] Maya Patel: Hosted has typical uptimes and Dedicated can get SLA add-ons; for POC we'll set internal SLOs for latency/availability and then discuss contractual SLAs if you move to Dedicated or Private.
[04:56] Anika Rao: practical question: how long is a representative benchmark run and what data do you need from us?
[05:05] Jorge Alvarez: recommend 48-72 hours for an initial burn-rate estimate and one shorter 2-4 hour peak stress run; we need your prompt sets, a 24h traffic trace (or synthetic mix) and expected concurrency distribution.
[05:20] Maya Patel: timeline suggestion: deliver harness by 6/2, ingest prompts by 6/4, run baseline hosted run 6/5-6/6, then run dedicated equivalent 6/8-6/10 if you want to compare.
[05:36] Priya Menon: will you provide encryption details for Private? we require KMS integration, HSM option, and key rotation policies.
[05:46] Jorge Alvarez: yes we'll include KMS/HSM whitepaper and a matrix of supported integrations; note hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS in many cloud providers.
[05:58] Anika Rao: what about model variants — are you suggesting base transformer quantized or smaller family? we need quality parity checks.
[06:08] Jorge Alvarez: we'll propose 2–3 model pairings: high-fidelity (fp16), quantized T4-friendly variant, and a lower-cost distilled option. we'll run model A/B and show quality delta vs cost.
[06:24] Tom Berger: curious on network egress cost for hosted runs — does Redwood pass through large egress or is that included?
[06:33] Maya Patel: egress is billed by cloud provider; we provide estimations, for Dedicated you can colocate to reduce it. we'll include egress estimates in the cost worksheet.
[06:46] Anika Rao: ok let's talk acceptance criteria again — if a hosted run meets latency but cost is higher than target, would you recommend dedicated?
[06:55] Jorge Alvarez: generally yes, dedicated often wins on cost per token at scale due to reserved capacity and lower per-token overhead; hosted wins on time-to-value. we'll quantify exactly in the burn-rate report.
[07:10] Priya Menon: i wanted to flag procurement timeline — security signoff and legal review will take 3-5 weeks once we decide on Dedicated/Private.
[07:20] Maya Patel: good to know. we'll align POC so critical vendor security items are validated early.
[07:28] Anika Rao: can you show a sample benchmark report?
[07:33] Jorge Alvarez: yes i'll attach a sample PDF in the followup — it shows latency distribution, tokens per request, cost model, and warm/cold cache diffs.
[07:45] Tom Berger: in terms of instrumentation, we'll need a small sidecar to route traffic for RPS shaping; is that supported?
[07:54] Jorge Alvarez: supported — the harness includes a lightweight traffic generator and sidecar configs.
[08:02] Maya Patel: ok moving to decision heuristics — quick checklist: if latency is critical and you need <100ms p50, dedicated co-located is likely; if time to market is critical and scale unknown, start hosted; if compliance/regulatory constraints exist choose private and plan for longer lead time.
[08:28] Anika Rao: for our immediate POC, we want to validate functional quality, burn-rate at our expected scale (peaks of 250), and prove path to private for enterprise customers.
[08:40] Maya Patel: perfect. that maps to doing hosted baseline then dedicated comparison, and document path for private in parallel.
[08:49] Priya Menon: please include audit log samples and retention controls in the security pack.
[08:56] Jorge Alvarez: will do.
[09:00] Maya Patel: ok lets confirm timeline and owners — i've put that in the action items. any blockers?
[09:06] Tom Berger: no blockers on infra side.
[09:09] Anika Rao: none, just need prompt set prep.
[09:11] Priya Menon: none, will review security doc.
[09:14] Maya Patel: cool. quick Q — competitors: do you want comparisons vs anthropic or vertex?
[09:20] Anika Rao: yes please if you have public perf numbers, specially around p99 for chat workloads.
[09:26] Jorge Alvarez: we'll include a high-level competitor appendix (public data only).
[09:32] Maya Patel: wrapping up — next steps again: jorge sends harness + sample report, anika sends prompts + trace, maya sends preliminary quote and scheduling.
[09:45] Anika Rao: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:48] Tom Berger: thanks.
[09:50] Priya Menon: thanks.
[09:52] Jorge Alvarez: talk soon.
[10:00] END OF CALL (actual duration ~62m)
